tagline: Four Grand Slams, one long season, and a new rivalry after the golden era.
why: Tennis is a global individual sport with a year-round tour, and its biggest events (the four Grand Slams) are cultural moments. After two decades of Federer, Nadal and Djokovic, a new generation led by Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz has taken over. It's an easy sport to talk about because the storylines are personal: rivalries, comebacks, ageing champions and rising stars.

essentials.title: The four Grand Slams
essentials.body: Australian Open (January, hard court), French Open or Roland Garros (May-June, clay), Wimbledon (July, grass) and the US Open (August-September, hard court). Slam titles are how careers are measured.

essentials.title: Surfaces change everything
essentials.body: Clay is slow with high bounces, rewarding grinders like Nadal. Grass is fast and low, rewarding big serves. Hard courts sit in between. Players often have a favourite surface.

essentials.title: Scoring is weird
essentials.body: Points go 15, 30, 40, game. 'Love' means zero, 'deuce' is 40-40. Six games win a set (by two), with a tiebreak at 6-6. Men play best-of-five sets at Slams; women best-of-three.

essentials.title: Two tours
essentials.body: The ATP runs men's tennis and the WTA runs women's. Players earn ranking points; the world number one is a big deal.

essentials.title: The Big Three era is over
essentials.body: Federer (20 Slams), Nadal (22) and Djokovic (24, the record) dominated from 2003 onward. Federer retired in 2022, Nadal in 2024, and Djokovic is in his late thirties.

essentials.title: Sinner vs Alcaraz
essentials.body: The two young stars split all eight Slams in 2024 and 2025 between them. Their matches, including the epic 2025 French Open final, are the new must-watch rivalry.

names.name: Novak Djokovic
names.what: Serbian with a record 24 men's Slam titles and the most weeks at number one. Won Olympic gold in 2024.

names.name: Rafael Nadal
names.what: Spanish legend with 22 Slams, 14 of them at the French Open. Retired in 2024.

names.name: Roger Federer
names.what: Swiss maestro with 20 Slams, beloved for his graceful style. Retired in 2022.

names.name: Jannik Sinner
names.what: Italian world number one with multiple Slams, including Wimbledon 2025. Served a three-month doping ban in 2025 that divided opinion.

names.name: Carlos Alcaraz
names.what: Spanish superstar with a flashy all-court game, multiple Slams on all three surfaces by age 22.

names.name: Aryna Sabalenka
names.what: Belarusian powerhouse and women's number one, a multiple Slam champion.

names.name: Iga Świątek
names.what: Polish star with four French Open titles who won Wimbledon in 2025.

names.name: Coco Gauff
names.what: American who won the 2023 US Open and 2025 French Open.

names.name: Serena Williams
names.what: 23 Slam singles titles; one of the greatest athletes ever. Retired in 2022.

names.name: Zheng Qinwen
names.what: China's top player, who won Olympic gold in Paris in 2024.

names.name: Li Na
names.what: The first Asian player to win a singles Slam (French Open 2011, Australian Open 2014).

names.name: Coleman Wong
names.what: Hong Kong's best men's player in a generation, breaking into the top 200 and beyond.

names.name: Andy Murray
names.what: British two-time Wimbledon champion, later Djokovic's coach for a spell.

timeline.event: The Open Era begins, letting professionals play the Slams.
Borg vs McEnroe Wimbledon final, one of the greatest matches ever.
Steffi Graf wins the Golden Slam.
Federer wins his first Wimbledon, starting the Big Three era.
Nadal beats Federer in the Wimbledon final in near-darkness.
Li Na becomes the first Asian Slam singles champion.
Djokovic beats Federer in an epic Wimbledon final after Federer had two match points.
Nadal retires; Zheng Qinwen wins Olympic gold; Sinner and Alcaraz take two Slams each.
Alcaraz saves three match points to beat Sinner in a five-and-a-half-hour French Open final.

now.headline: Sinner vs Alcaraz
now.detail: The rivalry everyone talks about. People pick sides based on style: Sinner's precision or Alcaraz's flair.

now.headline: Djokovic chasing 25
now.detail: Can he win one more Slam to set a record that may never be beaten?

now.headline: Women's tennis is open
now.detail: Sabalenka, Świątek, Gauff and others share the big titles, so every Slam is unpredictable.

now.headline: The schedule fight
now.detail: Players complain the season is too long, and there's talk of a 'Premium Tour' reshaping the calendar.

now.headline: Doping controversies
now.detail: Sinner's and Świątek's short bans for contamination cases in 2024-25 split fans on whether they got off lightly.

local.headline: Hong Kong Tennis Open
local.detail: A WTA tournament at Victoria Park each autumn, plus an ATP event that returned in January 2024.

local.headline: Coleman Wong
local.detail: Hong Kong's rising star, the city's first man in decades to compete regularly at Slams.

local.headline: Asian swing
local.detail: Big events in Beijing, Shanghai, Tokyo and Wuhan each autumn are an easy trip from Hong Kong.

local.headline: Pickleball and padel
local.detail: Faster-to-learn racket sports have exploded in Hong Kong too, a natural tangent from tennis chat.

debates.question: Who's the greatest: Federer, Nadal or Djokovic?
debates.sides: Djokovic has the numbers, Nadal the clay record, Federer the style and popularity.

debates.question: Is Alcaraz or Sinner better?
debates.sides: Sinner is more consistent; Alcaraz has the higher peak and more variety.

debates.question: Should women play best-of-five at Slams?
debates.sides: Some say equal prize money should mean equal sets; others say it would hurt quality and scheduling.

debates.question: Is the grass season too short?
debates.sides: Only a few weeks of grass makes Wimbledon a lottery for some players.
